population:detail2022:MYEB3 (2021 Geogra.publication_evidence:
["These datasets contain the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series. These time series offer users a rich source of data from which to conduct further investigation and research. The series are updated annually as part of each mid-year estimates release.

These datasets build on the population estimates and components of change previously published by ONS covering the period 2011 to 2022, by adding the most recent data from the mid-2022 population estimates and incorporating population estimates for 2012 to 2021 revised in light of the 2021 census in England and Wales. This offers a complete and consistent time series of estimates at detailed level from mid-2011 to mid-2022.", "These datasets provide the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series for 2011-2022 and are consistent with the results of the 2021 Census.

These unrounded estimates are published to enable and encourage further calculations and analysis. However, the estimates should not be taken to be accurate to the level of detail provided.
More information on the accuracy of the estimates is available in the Quality and Methodology document. Appropriate methods of disclosure control have been applied to prevent inference of information relating to individuals.

The estimated resident population of an area includes all people who usually live there, whatever their nationality. People arriving into an area from outside the UK are only included in the population estimates if their total stay or intended stay in the UK is 12 months or more. Visitors and short-term migrants (those who enter the UK for 3 to 12 months for certain purposes) are not included. The components of change provided in the file relate to the usual resident population only and will not show, for example, short-term migrants as part of the international migration flow. Similarly, people who leave the UK are only excluded from the population estimates if they remain, or intend to remain, outside the UK for 12 months or more. This is consistent with the United Nations recommended definition of an international long-term migrant. Members of UK and non-UK armed forces stationed in the UK are included in the population and UK forces stationed outside the UK are excluded. Students are taken to be resident at their term time address.", "
Publication dates", "The data tables in this spreadsheet were originally published at 9.30am 15 July 2024. These tables replace data originally published on 23 November 2023 and incorporate update estimates of international migration for England and Wales.", "Population estimates and components of population change, for mid-2023, were published on 15 July 2024.", "Date published: 15th July 2024"]

["These datasets contain the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series. These time series offer users a rich source of data from which to conduct further investigation and research. The series are updated annually as part of each mid-year estimates release.

These datasets build on the population estimates and components of change previously published by ONS covering the period 2011 to 2023, by adding the most recent data from the mid-2024 population estimates and incorporating population estimates for 2022 and 2023 revised to account for updated international and internal migration. This offers a complete and consistent time series of estimates at detailed level from mid-2011 to mid-2024.", "These datasets provide the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series for 2011 to 2024 and are consistent with the results of the 2021 Census.

These unrounded estimates are published to enable and encourage further calculations and analysis. However, the estimates should not be taken to be accurate to the level of detail provided.
More information on the accuracy of the estimates is available in the Quality and Methodology document. Appropriate methods of disclosure control have been applied to prevent inference of
information relating to individuals.

The estimated resident population of an area includes all people who usually live there, whatever their nationality. People arriving into an area from outside the UK are only included in the population estimates if their total stay or intended stay in the UK is 12 months or more. Visitors and short-term migrants (those who enter the UK for 3 to 12 months for certain purposes) are not included. The components of change provided in the file relate to the usual resident population only and will not show, for example, short-term migrants as part of the international migration flow. Similarly, people who leave the UK are only excluded from the population estimates if they remain, or intend to remain, outside the UK for 12 months or more. This is consistent with the United Nations recommended definition of an international long-term migrant. Members of UK and non-UK armed forces stationed in the UK are included in the population and UK forces stationed outside the UK are excluded. population.publication_evidence_json:
["These datasets contain the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series. These time series offer users a rich source of data from which to conduct further investigation and research. The series are updated annually as part of each mid-year estimates release.

These datasets build on the population estimates and components of change previously published by ONS covering the period 2011 to 2024, by adding the most recent data from the mid-2025 population estimates and incorporating population estimates for 2022, 2023 and 2024 revised to account for updated international migration. This offers a complete and consistent time series of estimates at detailed level from mid-2011 to mid-2025.", "These datasets provide the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series for 2011 to 2025 and are consistent with the results of the 2021 Census.

These unrounded estimates are published to enable and encourage further calculations and analysis. However, the estimates should not be taken to be accurate to the level of detail provided.
More information on the accuracy of the estimates is available in the Quality and Methodology Guide. Appropriate methods of disclosure control have been applied to prevent inference of information relating to individuals.

The estimated resident population of an area includes all people who usually live there, whatever their nationality. People arriving into an area from outside the UK are only included in the population estimates if their total stay or intended stay in the UK is 12 months or more. Visitors and short-term migrants (those who enter the UK for 3 to 12 months for certain purposes) are not included. The components of change provided in the file relate to the usual resident population only and will not show, for example, short-term migrants as part of the international migration flow. Similarly, people who leave the UK are only excluded from the population estimates if they remain, or intend to remain, outside the UK for 12 months or more. This is consistent with the United Nations recommended definition of an international long-term migrant. Members of UK and non-UK armed forces stationed in the UK are included in the population and UK forces stationed outside the UK are excluded. Students are taken to be resident at their term time address.", "
Publication dates", "The data tables in this spreadsheet were originally published at 9.30am 29 July 2026.", "Date published: 29 July 2026"]

population.publication_evidence_json:
["These datasets contain the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series. These time series offer users a rich source of data from which to conduct further investigation and research. The series are updated annually as part of each mid-year estimates release.

These datasets build on the population estimates and components of change previously published by ONS covering the period 2011 to 2022, by adding the most recent data from the mid-2022 population estimates and incorporating population estimates for 2012 to 2021 revised in light of the 2021 census in England and Wales. This offers a complete and consistent time series of estimates at detailed level from mid-2011 to mid-2022.", "These datasets provide the most detailed population estimates and components of change for the mid-year population series for 2011-2022 and are consistent with the results of the 2021 Census.

These unrounded estimates are published to enable and encourage further calculations and analysis. However, the estimates should not be taken to be accurate to the level of detail provided.
More information on the accuracy of the estimates is available in the Quality and Methodology document. Appropriate methods of disclosure control have been applied to prevent inference of information relating to individuals.

The estimated resident population of an area includes all people who usually live there, whatever their nationality. People arriving into an area from outside the UK are only included in the population estimates if their total stay or intended stay in the UK is 12 months or more. Visitors and short-term migrants (those who enter the UK for 3 to 12 months for certain purposes) are not included. The components of change provided in the file relate to the usual resident population only and will not show, for example, short-term migrants as part of the international migration flow. Similarly, people who leave the UK are only excluded from the population estimates if they remain, or intend to remain, outside the UK for 12 months or more. This is consistent with the United Nations recommended definition of an international long-term migrant. Members of UK and non-UK armed forces stationed in the UK are included in the population and UK forces stationed outside the UK are excluded. Students are taken to be resident at their term time address.", "
Publication dates", "The data tables in this spreadsheet were originally published at 9.30am 15 July 2024. These tables replace data originally published on 23 November 2023 and incorporate update estimates of international migration for England and Wales.", "Population estimates and components of population change, for mid-2023, were published on 15 July 2024.", "Date published: 15th July 2024"]

housing.text:
